brief: Goldman's Louis Miller argues that agentic AI lowers the cost of comparing, renegotiating, switching and cancelling, which erodes the switching friction many consumer businesses depend on, so profit pools built on customer inaction could come under pressure. The GSXUSWCH basket selects industries where stickiness comes from the effort of taking action rather than product differentiation: insurance, telecom, travel, subscriptions, marketplaces and certain fintech. If agents cut the cost of comparison and execution, pricing power, retention rates and customer lifetime value are what comes under pressure. The note gives two expressions, not one: short GSXUSWCH against the sector neutral GSCBHSCW hedge, which controls for beta and momentum, or limited loss put spreads out to January. The indicative example is the GSXUSWCH 15Jan27 90% 75% put spread at 1.81% ref 96.68, 8.3x max gross payout and 11.81% breakeven, buying the 21 delta at 27 vol and selling the 3 delta at 31.02 vol. The pair is a 10v trade sized -$10m/$10m, 57% specific risk and 29% industry bets. The note asserts in a chart caption that consumer inertia has already underperformed non-AI stocks year to date, without giving figures.
